newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish Conservative chief admits drink-drive crash.
newsitem.headline: Danish Conservative chief admits drink-drive crash.

text.p: Hans Engell, leader of Denmark's opposition Conservative party, said on Thursday that the party had asked him to remain in his post despite a car accident in which his blood-alcohol level was found to be well over the legal limit.
A party spokeswoman told Reuters that Engell veered off a motorway north of the capital and hit a lamp post on Wednesday night while driving his Mazda 626 car. He was unhurt.
He reported the accident to police and an alcohol test showed him to have a level of 1.37 percent. The legal limit is 0.8 percent and is shortly to be lowered to 0.5.
"I am deeply troubled by this incident and very sorry that it happened," Engell said in a statement.
He said that he had offered his resignation but the party's governing committees had asked him to stay on for the time being as party chairman and leader of the parliamentary Conservative group.
"In the light of this strong backing I have decided to remain in both posts. Beyond that I have no comment on the matter," he said.
A former journalist, he served as defence minister from 1982-87 and justice minister from 1989-93.

His Conservative party has less support than the main opposition Liberals but the two are allied in attempts to oust the ruling Social Democrat-led coalition and polls indicate that they would form the largest bloc if an election were held now.
General elections are scheduled to be held by September 1998.
